text.p: Italian debt markets ended strongly despite a slide in the lira against the mark, with bonds buoyed by firm U.S. markets, traders said.

Earlier bounce in the lira was deflated by comments from Germany's Juergen Stark, state secretary to the Finance Ministry, who said some countries would be well advised to delay entry into Europe's single currency, due to start in 1999.

The market took his comment to mean country's like Italy. But at the same time Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi was working to counter German concerns, saying Italy could move its 1998 budget forward several months to boost confidence.
The July 2006 Btp 25 basis points higher at the close at 110.92 while the November 2006 climbed 32 to 104.78.
The March future on LIFFE was 36 basis points up at 131.93 while the lira was quoted at 980.60/1.10 per mark after a day's peak of 970.50 per mark earlier.

Prodi proposed moving the deadline for parliamentary passage of the 1998 budget forward by four months to mid-August to boost confidence. He said this would reassure financial markets that Italy was serious about putting its finances in order and give "German voters and the German political world a pretty long time" to consider the country's merits.
The Italian Treasury's 18-month auction of zero coupon CTZs was undersubscribed, with bids and allocations of 1.68 trillion lire against the 2.50 trillion lire on offer in the auction.
